summary: xs-rs now packs small DATA records across directory NEEDs instead of flushing one tiny DATA frame per NEED, and automatic compression no longer spends zstd on kilobyte-sized listings. On a 2-CPU, 11 ms-RTT race of the congress-sample update-10pct shape it improved from 1.61 s to 1.43 s against the parent binary, with CPU down about 13%. Explicit -z still compresses every listing as before.
diagnosis: On a local fakessh pipe xs-rs was already faster, so I reproduced the lab shape with two-CPU affinity and an 11 ms relay. The update path was sending roughly one DATA frame per NEED (about 2,500 DATA frames for ~20 MiB of changed data) because each worker flushed its block at the end of every read task, even when the task held one small file. Under the same latency, auto-compression also spent zstd frames on nearly 10,000 small DIR listings. The parent measured 1.61 s wall / 0.63 s CPU with the lab update shape; the candidate 1.43 s / 0.55 s.
change: In rs/xs-rs/src/transfer.rs, workers now keep a partial DATA block across NEEDs and flush it at 256 KiB, at a skip-compress boundary, or when the worker has no more reads. DATA_END is emitted by the last worker after every worker has flushed, so no DATA can follow it. Automatic compression now compresses a DIR body only when it is at least 16 KiB; explicit -z still compresses all listings as xs-c++ does. Added a workers.rs regression test for 300 one-file directories plus a changed second pass.
expected_effect: Fewer DATA frames and fewer per-frame checksums, queue operations and writes on update-heavy trees, plus less CPU on small listings. In the local lab-shaped A/B this was 0.88x-0.91x the parent wall time and about 13% less CPU.
risks: Batching can delay a partial DATA block by up to 256 KiB per worker, and DATA_END now depends on all workers reporting their flush; this ordering is covered by the new test and the existing interop suite. Skipping automatic compression of small listings trades a little wire size for CPU; -z and explicitly requested compression are unchanged, and frames remain wire-compatible.
tests: Added a_worker_batches_small_one_file_directories_and_still_ends_cleanly. Ran XS_BIN=parent/build/xs cargo test --manifest-path rs/Cargo.toml (all unit, interop, delta, resume, xattr, ACL, workers tests pass), cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, and cargo clippy --all-targets --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu -D warnings; all pass.
commit_title: Batch DATA across NEEDs and skip tiny auto-compressed listings
commit_body:
Update-heavy trees ask for one small file per NEED, so flushing at the end of every read task sent about 2,500 tiny DATA frames for 20 MiB of changed data. Keep a partial DATA block per sender worker across NEEDs, flush it at 256 KiB, and have the last worker send DATA_END after all workers have flushed. Automatic compression now leaves DIR listings under 16 KiB raw; explicit -z still compresses every listing. Add a regression test with 300 one-file directories and a changed second pass.

On a 2-CPU, 11 ms-RTT congress-sample update-10pct race this cuts xs-rs wall from 1.61 s to 1.43 s and CPU from 0.63 s to 0.55 s versus the parent binary. The four gate commands pass.
